title: Successful User Registration with Valid Data
description: Verifies users can successfully register a portal account by submitting correct and complete personal information. This ensures only eligible users, meeting all required validation rules, can initiate their account and receive verification. Automation: HIGH — pure API assertions.
testDescription: A prospective user submits a registration form with all valid, synthetically generated personal details. Upon successful submission, the system creates an account and sends an email verification token, enforcing unique email and strong password rules as defined by compliance.
prerequisites: No account exists for email 'test+1001@example.com'; all registration field values generated to meet required formats; system accessible via HTTPS; email verification service operational.
stepsToPerform: 1. Open registration endpoint POST /v2/auth/register via HTTPS. 2. Enter first_name: 'Jane' (min 2, max 50 chars, alpha). 3. Enter last_name: 'Doe' (min 2, max 50 chars, alpha). 4. Enter email: 'test+1001@example.com' (RFC 5322, unique). 5. Enter password: 'TestPassword#2024' (min 12 chars, 1 upper, 1 lower, 1 digit, 1 symbol). 6. Enter date_of_birth: '2001-04-10' (ISO 8601, age >=18). 7. Enter phone_number: '+14165550101' (E.164 format). 8. Enter ssn_last4: '1234' (exactly 4 digits). 9. Set agree_terms: true. 10. Submit registration request. 11. Observe HTTP 201 response with 'user_id' and 'verification_token'. 12. Confirm email verification workflow triggered for given email.
expectedResult: 201 HTTP status returned. Response contains user_id and verification_token. Registration triggers email verification workflow as specified. No fields fail validation and email is unique in system.

sourceCitation.excerpt: POST/v2/auth/register Creates a new portal user account. Triggers email verification workflow.

title: Registration Failure due to Duplicate Email
description: Ensures registration is rejected if user submits an email already registered, preventing duplicate accounts and enforcing uniqueness. Protects against identity fraud and data duplication. Automation: HIGH — pure API assertions.
testDescription: A user attempts to register with an email address ('test+1002@example.com') that already exists in the system, submitting otherwise valid details. The registration must fail with a documented error code, preventing account creation.
prerequisites: An account already exists for email 'test+1002@example.com'; registration field values prepared as valid. No system outage or lockout.
stepsToPerform: 1. Confirm existing account for 'test+1002@example.com'. 2. Open registration endpoint POST /v2/auth/register. 3. Enter valid first_name, last_name, password, date_of_birth, phone_number, ssn_last4 as in TC-REG-01. 4. Enter email: 'test+1002@example.com' (RFC 5322 format, but not unique). 5. Set agree_terms: true. 6. Submit registration request. 7. Observe HTTP 409 error response. 8. Validate error code is 'EMAIL_EXISTS'. 9. Ensure no duplicate account is created. 10. Confirm system does not trigger email verification workflow.
expectedResult: HTTP 409 status returned. Response body includes error: EMAIL_EXISTS. No new account is created; email verification not triggered for duplicate email.

sourceCitation.excerpt: 409 Email already registered error: EMAIL_EXISTS

title: Boundary Validation for Password Complexity
description: Validates password boundary rules during registration, ensuring only passwords meeting minimum complexity are accepted and weaker values are rejected precisely per source criteria. Guards against weak credential risk. Automation: HIGH — API assertions.
testDescription: User attempts registration with boundary passwords: one exactly at complexity minimum (12 chars, correct composition), one violating each component (e.g. missing symbol or digit), and one just below minimum length (11 chars). Each submission must be accepted or rejected according to complexity rules.
prerequisites: No account exists for test email 'test+1003@example.com'; system ready for fresh registration; all other fields valid. Pass/Fail boundaries clearly enumerated.
stepsToPerform: 1. Open registration endpoint POST /v2/auth/register. 2. Enter valid first_name, last_name, date_of_birth, phone_number, ssn_last4, agree_terms. 3. Enter email: 'test+1003@example.com'. 4. Submit with password: 'Aa1!bcdefghij' (min 12, 1 upper, 1 lower, 1 digit, 1 symbol) and expect success. 5. Submit with password: 'Aa1bcdefghij' (missing symbol), expect error 'WEAK_PASSWORD'. 6. Submit with password: 'AA1!bcdefghij' (missing lower), expect error 'WEAK_PASSWORD'. 7. Submit with password: 'aa1!bcdefghij' (missing upper), expect error 'WEAK_PASSWORD'. 8. Submit with password: 'Aa1!bcdefghi' (11 chars, all composition met), expect error 'WEAK_PASSWORD'. 9. Confirm correct error in response for each negative boundary attempt. 10. For successful submission, confirm 201 status and email verification initiated.
expectedResult: Registration accepted only with password 'Aa1!bcdefghij' (meets all rules). All other tested boundaries return HTTP 422 and error: WEAK_PASSWORD. No account is created for failed inputs. Error message matches documentation.

sourceCitation.excerpt: password String Required Min 12 chars; 1 upper, 1 lower, 1 digit, 1 symbol

title: Successful Login with MFA Enabled
description: Verifies login succeeds with both credentials and correct MFA code when MFA is enabled, enforcing multi-factor controls for enhanced account security. Protects against unauthorized access. Automation: HIGH — API assertions.
testDescription: A registered user with MFA enabled attempts to log in, supplying correct email, password, and six-digit TOTP. If all values are correct, system issues access and refresh tokens, starting a new session.
prerequisites: User account exists for 'test+1004@example.com'; MFA enabled; known valid TOTP code present; account not locked.
stepsToPerform: 1. Access login endpoint POST /v2/auth/login. 2. Enter email: 'test+1004@example.com'. 3. Enter password: 'TestPassword#2024'. 4. Retrieve current TOTP code for MFA ('123456'; must be valid for session). 5. Enter mfa_code: '123456'. 6. Optionally submit device_id (UUID v4). 7. Optionally set remember_me: false. 8. Submit login request. 9. Observe HTTP 200 response. 10. Confirm presence of access_token, refresh_token, expires_in in response. 11. Ensure token TTL is 15 min unless remember_me is true.
expectedResult: HTTP 200 status returned. Response includes access_token, refresh_token, and expires_in. No error returned. Access is granted only with correct MFA code. Session started securely.

sourceCitation.excerpt: mfa_code String Optional 6-digit TOTP if MFA enabled on account

title: Account Lockout after Five Failed Login Attempts
description: Verifies account lockout occurs after five consecutive failed login attempts as documented, enforcing brute-force mitigation and user protection measures. Automation: HIGH — API assertions.
testDescription: A user attempts to log in with incorrect password five times in a row. On the sixth attempt, the system must reject login and return an account lockout error, including unlock_at timestamp.
prerequisites: User account exists for 'test+1005@example.com' with MFA disabled; account is not locked; known valid password but test will use incorrect password.
stepsToPerform: 1. Access login endpoint POST /v2/auth/login. 2. Enter valid email: 'test+1005@example.com'. 3. Enter incorrect password: 'WrongPass001'. 4. Submit login request; observe 401 INVALID_CREDENTIALS. 5. Repeat steps 2-4 five times (total: 5 failed attempts). 6. Attempt sixth login with any password (even if correct). 7. Submit login request. 8. Observe HTTP 403 response. 9. Confirm error code is ACCOUNT_LOCKED. 10. Validate unlock_at timestamp is present in response. 11. Attempt login after unlock_at; confirm system allows login.
expectedResult: Sixth login attempt returns HTTP 403 with error: ACCOUNT_LOCKED, unlock_at. Account prevented from login until unlock_at time. No tokens issued while locked.

sourceCitation.excerpt: 403 Account locked after 5 failed attempts error: ACCOUNT_LOCKED, unlock_at

title: Token Refresh with Valid Refresh Token
description: Verifies users can obtain a new access token using a valid, single-use refresh token, enforcing token rotation and session continuity per compliance. Automation: HIGH — API assertions.
testDescription: An authenticated user submits a valid refresh token (obtained from prior login) to the token refresh endpoint. System must return a new access token and rotate the refresh token. Old refresh token is invalidated and cannot be reused.
prerequisites: User account exists; valid access_token and refresh_token pair obtained from login; refresh_token not expired nor previously used.
stepsToPerform: 1. Log in to obtain access_token and refresh_token for 'test+1007@example.com'. 2. Store refresh_token securely. 3. Wait for access_token to approach expiry (<15 min TTL). 4. Post to /v2/auth/token/refresh with refresh_token. 5. Observe HTTP 200 response. 6. Confirm new access_token and new refresh_token returned. 7. Attempt to reuse old refresh_token; observe HTTP 401 TOKEN_INVALID. 8. Confirm session continuity with new access_token (test protected endpoint). 9. Ensure rotation enforced and session not interrupted.
expectedResult: HTTP 200 status with new access_token and refresh_token returned. Old refresh token is invalidated. New token pair allows continued access. Rotation enforcement confirmed (old token fails).

sourceCitation.excerpt: POST/v2/auth/token/refresh Issues a new access token using a valid refresh token (rotation enforced).

title: Logout Invalidates Session Tokens
description: Verifies session tokens (access and refresh) are invalidated immediately upon user logout, preventing reuse and enforcing token expiry requirements per security standards. Automation: HIGH — API assertions.
testDescription: A logged-in user initiates logout. All session tokens must be invalidated, ensuring that subsequent API calls using old tokens are rejected and user is effectively signed out.
prerequisites: User is logged in; valid access_token and refresh_token in HttpOnly cookies; session active; no concurrent logouts.
stepsToPerform: 1. Obtain access_token and refresh_token for 'test+1008@example.com' via login. 2. Access logout endpoint (as per API spec; e.g., POST /v2/auth/logout if available). 3. Submit logout request (ensure X-CSRF-Token present if required). 4. Observe response confirming logout (HTTP 200 or similar). 5. Attempt API call to protected endpoint using access_token; expect rejection. 6. Attempt token refresh with refresh_token; expect HTTP 401 TOKEN_INVALID. 7. Attempt to view session-bound resources in portal; confirm access denied. 8. Observe session expiration and cookie clearing in browser. 9. Ensure session cannot be restored without fresh authentication.
expectedResult: Session tokens invalidated immediately upon logout. API calls using old access_token fail with authorization error. Refresh token unusable. User signed out securely; session cleared.

sourceCitation.excerpt: All API calls originate from the browser and are authenticated via JWT Bearer tokens with a 15-minute expiry and refresh token rotation.

title: Submit Financials and Trigger Credit Pull
description: This test verifies that users can submit required financial and employment information for a credit card application, triggering a soft credit pull with the correct data and enforcing mandatory field validation and session token handling. Automation: HIGH — pure API assertions.
testDescription: A user continues a credit application by submitting employment status, employer (if applicable), gross annual income, monthly rent, debts, and consent for SIN usage, ensuring that a credit bureau pull is triggered. System must respond with PENDING_REVIEW status and a FICO pull is queued. Failure to include required fields or a valid session token should block progression.
prerequisites: Valid application_id from successfully completed Step 1 (personal info), session_token issued and unexpired, user authenticated via JWT bearer token, all source-required fields available in test data.
stepsToPerform:
1. Start Step 1 and obtain a valid application_id and session_token.
2. Prepare financial data: employment_status: EMPLOYED, employer_name: 'Aegis Test Inc.', gross_annual_income: 85000.00, other_income: 5000.00, monthly_rent: 1800.00, existing_debt_payments: 300.00, sin_consent: true.
3. Construct POST request to /v2/applications/{application_id}/financials with all required fields in the request body.
4. Set X-App-Session header to the valid session_token.
5. Ensure all amounts are positive and correctly formatted per schema.
6. Submit the API request and record the response.
7. Verify that status code is 200 and response includes the keys: status: PENDING_REVIEW, fico_pull_id.
8. Confirm that a soft credit pull is initiated via downstream bureau API (mock or stub, if needed for automation).
9. Attempt the same request but with missing required field (e.g., omit employer_name when employment_status=EMPLOYED) and assert validation error occurs.
10. Attempt request with invalid session_token and observe SESSION_EXPIRED error.
11. Inspect the backend (or stub) to ensure the credit pull was queued with correct user and application reference.
expectedResult: 200 response code with body containing status: PENDING_REVIEW and fico_pull_id. A soft credit pull is initiated. If required fields or session_token are missing or invalid, appropriate error codes (400 or 401) and messages are returned. No sensitive data is leaked in logs/responses.

sourceCitation.excerpt: POST/v2/applications/{application_id}/financials Submits income and employment data. Triggers soft credit pull via bureau API.

sourceCitation.excerpt: 401 session_token expired or invalid error: SESSION_EXPIRED

title: Auto-Approved Application Based on FICO Score

The backend retrieves a FICO score > 680 via the credit bureau stub and must auto-approve the application, returning APPROVED status, a credit_limit, and a card_number_masked (last 4 digits visible only).

2. Retrieve or mock suitable card_product_id from /v2/products; e.g., 'AEGIS_GOLD'.

title: Over-Limit Transaction with Essential Service Buffer
description: This test checks that essential service transactions slightly exceeding the card's available credit (within a 5% buffer) are still approved and flagged over_limit, ensuring continuity for critical payments. Automation: HIGH — requires concrete test data and buffer calculation.
testDescription: A user attempts a payment that exceeds their available credit but falls within the defined 5% buffer for essential services. The system must approve the transaction, return over_limit_flag: true, and allow transaction completion.
prerequisites: User authenticated, account_id with available_credit = $1000.00, card_status = Active, test merchant classified as essential service by mcc_code, test within buffer limit.
stepsToPerform:
1. Query available_credit for account_id; set up so available_credit is exactly $1000.00.

title: Duplicate Notification Prevented via Idempotency Key
description: This test verifies that multiple webhook requests with the same idempotency_key do not trigger duplicate notifications, and the system responds with correct error codes. Automation: HIGH — API and log assertions.
testDescription: A notification webhook is submitted twice for the same account_id, alert_type, channel, message_body, and idempotency_key. The first request is delivered, the second should be rejected with 'DUPLICATE_NOTIFICATION'.
prerequisites: account_id exists, valid idempotency_key (UUID v4: 1e90xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx44c88a7), notification engine active, alert webhook endpoint accessible, channel delivery roles provisioned.
stepsToPerform: 1. Craft webhook payload with account_id: test-acc-002, alert_type: STATEMENT_READY, channel: PUSH, message_body: 'Your statement is ready.', severity: INFO, idempotency_key: 1e90xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx44c88a7. 2. Send POST /v2/notifications/webhook. 3. Assert 200 response, notification_id, delivered_at. 4. Verify notification received in PUSH channel. 5. Resend identical webhook payload to same endpoint (same idempotency_key). 6. Observe response: HTTP 409, error: DUPLICATE_NOTIFICATION. 7. Inspect notification channel to confirm only one alert received. 8. Repeat with alternate alert_type; use new idempotency_key, confirm delivery. 9. Test different account_id with original idempotency_key—should not be treated as duplicate. 10. Validate all delivery logs show single notification per idempotency_key per account/channel. 11. Attempt concurrent delivery (send 10 identical requests in rapid succession), assert only one delivered, all others rejected. 12. Confirm idempotency enforced across network retries and error scenarios.
expectedResult: Webhook endpoint returns 409 DUPLICATE_NOTIFICATION for repeated idempotency_key, only one alert delivered per key per account/channel, delivery logs show single entry. No duplicate alerts sent even under concurrency/fail/retry.

title: Full User Journey: Registration to Account Closure
description: This test covers the complete lifecycle of a user: from registration, application, approval, card activation, transaction, statement, payment, notification, to account closure. It verifies all workflow boundaries, states, and compliance controls. Automation: MEDIUM — spans UI/API with session and audit checks.
testDescription: A new user registers, completes multi-step credit application, receives approval and masked card, activates card, performs a transaction, receives relevant notifications, retrieves statement, makes a payment, and finally closes the account within allowed window. All required business, compliance, and audit rules are tested in sequence.
prerequisites: No prior user with same email, full application flow enabled, card products provisioned, test merchant available, notification and billing systems operational, audit log access, account closure endpoint enabled, current date within 14 days post-issuance.
stepsToPerform: 1. Register user via POST /v2/auth/register with email: test+e2e01@example.com, password: 'E2eStrong!2026', ssn_last4: 4321, date_of_birth: 1992-06-17, agree_terms: true. 2. Confirm 201 response with user_id, verification_token. 3. Complete email verification. 4. Start credit application (Step 1): submit personal info, obtain application_id, session_token. 5. Submit financial info (Step 2): employment_status: EMPLOYED, gross_income: 85000, monthly_rent: 1200, sin_consent: true. 6. Finalize application (Step 3): card_product_id: AEGIS_GOLD, e_signature: 'TestUser', marketing_opt_in: false. 7. Confirm decision: APPROVED, receive masked card_number, credit_limit. 8. Activate card, set PIN: new_pin: 1234, confirm_pin: 1234, session_otp: 766219. 9. Perform a purchase transaction: merchant_name: 'TestBooks', mcc_code: 5942, amount: $20.50. 10. Verify transaction approved; available_credit updated. 11. Receive notification: OVER_LIMIT (for test), IN_APP and email alerts observed. 12. Retrieve statement for billing cycle; confirm statement accuracy. 13. Make payment: payment_amount: $20.50, payment_type: STATEMENT_BALANCE, bank_account_id: test-bank-001. 14. Confirm payment accepted, new balance estimate. 15. Delete account within 14 days using DELETE /v2/accounts/{id}. 16. Confirm account closure response, audit logs show full life-cycle, session invalidated.
expectedResult: User flows seamlessly through registration, application, card activation, transaction, statement, payment, and closure. Each stage triggers correct responses, notifications, audits, and data masking. Account closure succeeds if within 14 days, session terminated, all related records are logged and retrievable for compliance.
